'''''Lavandula multifida''''', the '''fernleaf lavender'''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Lavandula multifida - Plant Finder |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281617 |access-date=2023-04-29 |website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}}</ref> or '''Egyptian lavender''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lavandula multifida {{!}} Egyptian lavender Shrubs/RHS Gardening |url=http://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/25423/lavandula-multifida/details |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=www.rhs.org.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> is a small plant, sometimes a shrub, native to the southern regions of the [[Mediterranean]], including [[Iberian Peninsula|Iberia]], [[Sicily]], Northwest Africa and the [[Canary Islands]].

The plant grows up to {{Convert|24|in|cm|abbr=on}} tall.<ref name=":0" /> The stems are grey and woolly. Leaves are fernlike, double pinnate and silver to green in colour.<ref name=":0" /> Dark blue or violet flowers may be either single or three-pronged,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-12 |title=Lavandula multifida (Fern Leaf Lavender) |url=https://mymediterraneangarden.com/plants/lavandula-multifida/ |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=My Mediterranean Garden |language=en-GB}}</ref> and are borne on long stems held above the foliage.

''L. multifida'' is grown both as a [[herb]] and as an [[ornamental plant]]. Foliage is aromatic, but it has been noted that the scent is closer to that of [[oregano]] than to other kinds of lavender.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lavandula multifida {{!}} Egyptian lavender Shrubs/RHS Gardening |url=http://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/25423/lavandula-multifida/details |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=www.rhs.org.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> In cooler latitudes it is killed by winter frost, but can be grown as an annual. Cultivars include 'Spanish Eyes'.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.plantoftheweek.org/week380.shtml |work=Cal's Plant of the Week |title=''Lavandula multifida'' 'Spanish Eyes' |publisher=University of Oklahoma Department of Botany & Microbiology |first=Cal |last=Lemke |date=October 2006 |access-date=2009-08-26 |archive-date=2008-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080225081632/http://www.plantoftheweek.org/week380.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref>
